title: Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC v2.1): Modular Synthesis across Structure, Dynamics, and Cognition
description: Formalizes Energy-Flow Cosmology v2.1 as a modular framework linking structural (halos in a Grid–Higgs medium), dynamical (energy flow–entropy–time relations), and cognitive (informational coupling) domains. Replaces dark components with a measurable energy-flow field Ef governed by entropic gradients, proposes a variable light velocity c(S) tied to energy density, and interprets the CMB as a steady-state thermodynamic equilibrium.

structural_field_relation.description: EFC-S field equation: entropic permeability k(S) and effective potential V(Ef,S) determine stationary halo configurations in the Grid–Higgs medium.

energy_flow_linear_law.description: EFC-D fundamental relation: energy flow decreases linearly with normalized entropy.

temporal_mapping.description: Emergent time mapping: apparent curvature in Ef(t) arises from an exponential growth of entropy with time.

variable_light_velocity.description: Light speed emerges from GH medium properties, inversely related to local energy density; locally constant, cosmologically variable.

cognitive_field_equation.description: EFC-C coupling: a reflective informational field co-varies with energy flow, entropy, and time, linking cognition to thermodynamic dynamics.

key_results.main_finding: Presents a unified, modular thermodynamic framework where a measurable energy-flow field Ef links structure, dynamics, and cognition, offering entropic alternatives to dark components and a steady-state interpretation of the CMB.
parameters_tested: Cognitive field coupling Ψ_CEM ∼ f(Ef, S, t) (Eq. 5)

sealed_predictions.statement: The effective speed of light c varies cosmologically and correlates inversely with large-scale energy density ρ(S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint constraints from high-redshift time-of-flight measurements of transients (FRBs, GRBs) after plasma-dispersion correction, plus spectral-line and fine-structure-constant measurements across redshift showing no correlated variation.

sealed_predictions.statement: Galaxy rotation curves and weak-lensing mass profiles can be reproduced from Eq. (1) using baryonic matter only via k(S) and V(Ef,S), without invoking non-baryonic dark matter.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: A representative galaxy/cluster sample where no physically plausible k(S), V(Ef,S) can simultaneously fit rotation curves and lensing maps given observed baryon distributions.

sealed_predictions.statement: The CMB arises from a steady-state thermodynamic equilibrium between S→0 emission and S→1 recirculation rather than a relic recombination surface.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: CMB temperature/polarization spectra whose acoustic peak phases, damping tail, and TE/EE correlations unambiguously require a recombination-era last-scattering surface and are irreconcilable with steady-state recirculation.

sealed_predictions.statement: Offsets between mass and baryons in merging clusters (e.g., Bullet-like systems) are reproducible as entropy-gradient responses within Eq. (1) without dark matter.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Robust lensing/baryon maps of multiple mergers demonstrating systematic mass–baryon separations that cannot be produced by any solution of Eq. (1) with physically admissible k(S) and V(Ef,S).

kill_criteria: KC1: Direct detection of non-baryonic dark matter with properties (abundance, interaction cross-section, and clustering) that quantitatively account for galaxy/cluster dynamics and lensing without room for the entropic-halo mechanism of Eq. (1).

KC2: Cosmological and local constraints demonstrating that c is constant to a level that excludes any viable c(S) ∝ 1/ρ(S) variation sufficient to impact large-scale dynamics (e.g., null time-of-flight, spectral-line, and fine-structure-constant evolution across redshift inconsistent with Eq. (4)).

KC3: Inability of Eq. (1), for any physically reasonable k(S) and V(Ef,S), to reproduce both rotation curves and weak/strong lensing profiles across a statistically significant galaxy and cluster sample using only observed baryons.

KC4: CMB observations whose temperature and polarization spectra (including acoustic peak phases, damping tail, and TE/EE correlations) are demonstrably incompatible with a steady-state equilibrium origin and can only be explained by a recombination-era last-scattering surface.

KC5: Demonstration that no parameterization of ρ(S) and k(S) can yield a locally constant yet cosmologically varying c(S) without violating precision Lorentz-invariance bounds or multi-messenger arrival-time constraints.
